best_human.method: Dual of the binary double-error-correcting BCH code, constructed from columns (alpha^i, alpha^(3i)) over GF(64) and all 4096 binary linear forms.
best_human.source: Carlet, Kiss, Nagy, Simplicity conditions for binary orthogonal arrays, https://doi.org/10.1007/s10623-022-01105-4, Remark 5.
best_human.evidence_state: All 637392 nonempty parity characters of sizes one through four are balanced exactly; this implies each 4-column pattern occurs 256 times.
best_human.ai_provenance: The cited method is a classical BCH-code construction. This local formula reconstruction is not described as the historical authors' computation; the source does not state AI use.

best_public.method: Shortened Kerdock-code construction; Carlet, Kiss, and Nagy state this gives 2^(2m-1) rows for 2^m-1 columns when m is even, including m=6.
best_public.evidence_state: Same-parameter 2048-row construction reported in the primary source. Its explicit rows were not reconstructed in this task.
best_public.ai_provenance: The source predates current AI-assisted records and does not state AI involvement.
best_public.optimality: The source states that optimality is not known. Rao and divisibility give lower bound 2032, leaving a 16-row gap.

best_reproduced.evidence_state: Independent parity-character checker confirms exact strength 4.
best_reproduced.origin_type: Local rebuild of the traditional BCH-dual construction.

best_own_search.origin_type: Task-local construction from the simple seed; comparison assets were not read.

details.pattern_equivalence: For each selected set of four columns, all nontrivial parity characters are balanced; binary Fourier inversion gives every 4-bit pattern exactly N/16 times.

best_own_search.evidence_state: Strict replay and independent Sol review passed; see acceptance.json.

source_review.optimality_status: Open in the primary source and no later closure was found in searches through 2026-11-06.
source_review.lower_bound: Rao bound 2017, plus N divisible by 16, gives 2032.
source_review.notes: The primary paper explicitly says optimality of the Kerdock construction is unknown. Searches for exact OA(2048,63,2,4) and F*(63,2,4) did not find a later proof.
